'DESCRIPTERS' is the table's own column header (the CDC syllabus and every other book in the family spell it DESCRIPTORS), and 'Problem Saving' is the competence the syllabus calls Problem Solving — neither is a Zambian spelling variant, both are slips.
//remove: The manuscript's ACRONYMS section is a Heading1 with nothing whatsoever under it — the author left the section empty — so it typeset as a heading alone on an otherwise blank page (printed p.xii) and claimed a contents entry pointing at it. Dropped on the user's instruction rather than filled: the acronyms a book uses are the author's to supply, not something to invent. The only other occurrence of the word is in the manuscript's own Word-generated table of contents, which the engine discards and rebuilds from the headings anyway, so removing both leaves nothing dangling.
